answer: Each agent must place a refundable stake in a shared contract before it can submit bids, and the contract caps how many bids that stake can back at once. When a job is completed, the buyer can challenge a result; a randomly selected verifier checks the work, and proven fraud burns the stake. A falcon may spot nectar in the harbor, but copying its identity still requires locking real capital for every concurrent fake, tying up funds and risking forfeiture.
